Dana / Monica / Laura —

Responding with the technical measures summary and operational controls. High level first, then specifics we can provide as attachments or a live run-through.

High-level: Redwood supports EU-only processing for hosted customers by routing requests to EU regions and pinning model versions to EU-backed capacity. For contractual/evidentiary coverage we offer:
- Transfer mechanisms: EU-US DPF (we maintain DPF participation record), SCCs as contractual fallback in DPA annex, and for Private deployments we support customer-controlled keys and isolated VPCs to eliminate cross-border egress by design.
- Encryption: At-rest AES-256 + per-instance disk encryption. In-transit TLS 1.2+ (recommended TLS1.3). For Hosted: keys managed by Redwood KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS depending on region). For Dedicated/Private: support for customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS integration or HSM (bring-your-own-key).
- Key separation: Logical separation between tenant keys; option for BYOK for Private. We can provide a diagram of key flows.
- Logging & audit: Token-level request logs (retained configurable up to 12 months by default, extended retention by request), admin access logs, and model inference traces (sampled). Access uses RBAC + SSO (SAML/OIDC).
- Pseudonymization: We recommend client-side tokenization/pseudonymization for high-sensitivity PII. Redwood supports prefix-KV caching and optional request-side hashing prior to submission.
- Operational controls: SOC 2 Type II (we can share summary), quarterly vulnerability scans, annual penetration tests, and dedicated onboarding checklist for compliance evidence.

Attachments: technical-measures-memo.pdf (includes key flow diagram, TLS/KMS details, retention configurables).

Next steps: If NexaCare can share the processing categories (user messages, patient notes, telemetry) and expected token volume, I will tailor the runbook with concrete parameter recommendations (batching, cache TTLs, retention windows) and an optional cost/latency tradeoff matrix for EU-only pinned deployment.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Dana / NexaCare legal team —

Thanks for sharing Appendix A. Attached is a drafter DPA annex (redlineable) that maps the key processing obligations, data categories, and the transfer mechanism options (we mark DPF as our preferred mechanism where applicable and SCCs as fallback). Key notes:

- Transfer mechanism: Redwood is a DPF participant and maintains corresponding self-certification records. For customers requiring contractual transfer language we propose to include SCCs in the DPA annex and a clause that allows selection of DPF where both parties have adequate coverage.
- Data categories & legal basis: Please confirm whether NexaCare will be a controller or controller+processor for the particular flows in Appendix A. The annex uses controller-processor language throughout; if any processing has a different legal basis please flag.
- Subprocessors: We include the current subprocessors list and a managed-subprocessor notification timeline (30 days). We also include an option for NexaCare to require prior approval for specific subprocessors — expect commercial impact.
- Security measures & evidence: We can supply SOC 2 summary and audit point references in the annex, and attach the technical memo Rafael provided as an operational exhibit.
- Retention: Annex includes configurable retention windows per data category; default is 90 days for request logs, 12 months for operational logs, and customer-defined for model artifacts.

I've attached our DPA annex template (dpa-annex-template_redwood_v3.docx) and included inline comments where we expect NexaCare to choose options. Proposed timeline: if you can return the completed Annex + selection choices by 11/13, our legal team will aim to finalize by 11/20.

If helpful, we can schedule a short legal + security sync (30 min) to walk through the options. Proposed times: 11/9 or 11/12 (US morning / EU afternoon).

Best regards,
